units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 12:7">Gen. R. s. 12</cite> <he>שלשה דברים הללו … שלש ת׳ וכ׳</he> the following three things form the real creations of the world, and each of them delayed three days, and then produced offspring: the earth &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 12:7">Ib.</cite> <he>לכל יש ת׳ … יש להן ת׳ וכ׳</he> all things have origins (mentioned in the Bible), heaven and earth have origins &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 12:7">Ib.</cite> <he>כל מי שיש לו ת׳ וכ׳</he> whatever has an origin, dies and decays, is created, but does not create, but that which has no origin does not die &c.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 14:12">Num. R. s. 14<sup>12</sup></cite> <he>בעת שהעמיד ת׳</he> during the time of his begetting children.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 8:3:7">Y. Sot. VIII, 22ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>שלישי לת׳ ורביעי וכ׳</he> he was the third in the order of birth, and the fourth in the order of accession; a. fr.

senses.gloss: secondary act, subspecies, opp. אב or עיקר, v. אָב II.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:5:6">Y. Sabb. II, 5ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>שחיטה עיקר וחבורה ת׳</he> slaughtering is the primary act (forbidden on the Sabbath), and wounding is the secondary act.
B. Kam. 2ᵃ הך … קרי לה ת׳ an act which was essential at the building of the Tabernacle is called ab, and one which was not essential, is called toladah; a. fr.—Pl. as ab.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 2a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>מדקתני אבות מכלל דאיכא ת׳</he> since the Mishnah speaks of main damages, we must conclude that there are also secondary ones; <he>תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶן כיוצא בהן וכ׳</he> are their subspecies subject to the same laws or not? <cite ref="Shabbat 2b:4-5">Sabb. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>הכא … תני אבות ותני ת׳ וכ׳</he> here (<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:1">Sabb. I, 1</cite>) where the main subject is the Sabbath, the Mishnah specifies the main act and the secondary acts, &c.; <cite ref="Shevuot 5a:15">Shebu. 5ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.
